notes: Zero: three-way signum returns 0 (C1,C4,C5,C6) vs two-way 'nonnegative is +1' (C3) vs sign-bit copysign where 0.0->1 (C2).
Negative zero: -0.0 collapses to 0 (C1,C4,C6), maps to -1 via sign bit (C2,C5).
NaN: silently 0 (C1,C5,C6), raises ValueError (C3,C4), or follows the sign bit -> 1 (C2).
Tiny values: exact comparison (all but C6) vs epsilon tolerance where |x|<=1e-9 counts as zero (C6).
Invalid types: C4 raises TypeError for bool/non-numeric; others accept anything comparable (True -> 1).
Infinity: all return +/-1 (via comparison or sign bit) — included to confirm no candidate rejects it.
Infinity: +inf/-inf have a sign (1/-1) vs. non-finite is rejected with ValueError just like NaN (candidates 3, 5).
Numeric strings like '3' or ' -2.5 ': coerced via float() and accepted (candidates 2, 5) vs. rejected as wrong type.
Near-zero values: exact comparison (1e-300 -> 1) vs. epsilon tolerance where |x| < 1e-9 counts as 0 (candidate 4).

Non-numeric input (None, 'abc'): TypeError (duck-typed comparison / float() failure) vs. ValueError 'not a real number' (candidate 6) vs. coercion failure remapped to TypeError even for unparsable strings (candidate 5).
NaN detection strategy: x != x duck typing vs. math.isnan/isfinite vs. float() coercion — changes which non-float types are accepted at all.
